key_insight: ViTamyloid uses vision foundation models to automatically segment and classify amyloid-β lesions in postmortem human brain slides, enabling more detailed lesion-level quantification than traditional semiquantitative scoring.
clinical_relevance: This could improve neuropathology workflows by providing more scalable, standardized assessment of Alzheimer’s disease-related amyloid pathology and vascular involvement.
method: Stage 1: EfficientNet-B4 U-Net plus Faster R-CNN to detect and separate amyloid lesion candidates.
Stage 2: Frozen UNI2-h pathology foundation model with a trainable ViT Adapter to classify lesions into five categories.
Validated across donor-disjoint splits and tested on independent datasets with different stains, scanners, resolutions, and image quality.
evidence_signal: The model achieved 0.903 donor-disjoint macro F1, with high AUROC/AUPRC across lesion classes and better performance than frozen features alone and prior pipelines.
watch_item: Performance was shown on retrospective digital pathology data, so real-world robustness may still depend on site-specific staining, scanning, and annotation variability.
paper_title: Generalizing Amyloid β Pathology from Postmortem Human Brains with Vision Foundation Models for Lesion Quantification
